channel.title: Inigo Angulo, writing
channel.description: Notes on building product with AI agent teams, conversion experiments and design systems.

item.title: AI agent teams for software development: what actually works in 2026
item.description: How to run a team of AI coding agents that ships to production: roles with mandates, isolation, gates, a decision log, and the numbers from seven weeks of doing it.

item.title: Human in the loop for coding agents: the two gates that matter
item.description: Where a person must sit when AI agents write and ship code: the decision gate (one id, one letter) and the release gate (one approval with a security report). Everything else can be automated.

item.title: 445 PRs in seven weeks: what a one person team with AI agents actually looks like
item.description: Real numbers from building Acervo with an AI engineering team: 484 pull requests, 1,456 CI runs, 15 gated releases, and what the human did all day.

item.title: Why a green check is not proof: the gates between an AI agent and production
item.description: On October 6 a navigation redesign merged on 8 of 8 green checks. The e2e job had not run. What that taught me about verification when agents write the code.

item.title: Checkout conversion: the ten experiments behind +11%
item.description: At GetYourGuide, 38% of converters left checkout and came back with no re-entry experience. Ten experiments, four EU markets, +11% conversion, and the ones that lost.

item.title: Row level security with AI agents: tests that run as the user who must not get in
item.description: How to keep multi tenant isolation honest when agents write the migrations: every rule lives in the database, every policy has a test that runs as the wrong user, and the reviewer breaks a policy on purpose.

item.title: How much does it cost to build an MVP with AI agents? Real numbers from one build
item.description: What a production MVP built with an AI agent team actually costs: the agent bill, the infrastructure, the human time, and where the money really goes. Numbers from seven weeks on Acervo.

item.title: Fractional product manager vs product consultant: which one do you actually need?
item.description: A consultant diagnoses and recommends. A fractional product manager owns outcomes inside your team for a period. How to tell which one your company needs, and what each should cost you.

item.title: A Figma design system that mirrors the codebase: tokens first, then components, then screens
item.description: How to build a design system so that Figma and code say the same thing: a single token source exported to CSS by script, a component library that consumes it, and checks that fail when a raw value sneaks in.

item.title: Instrument the gaps, not the stages: funnel analytics that find the real leak
item.description: Stage by stage funnels hide where people actually drop: the back button, the tab switch, the return visit. How to rebuild a funnel per user and find the leak nobody measured.

item.title: From ticket to production in five hours: a release process for a one person team
item.description: One real change, end to end: ticket at 14:35, pull request at 16:56, fourteen checks, pen test PASS, merge, promotion at 19:50, served at 19:54. The process that makes that routine and safe.
